newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan November offshore banking unit assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan November offshore banking unit assets rise.

text.p: The combined assets of Taiwan's 65 offshore banking units (OBUs) rose 4.0 percent to US$35.512 billion at the end of November from a year earlier, the central bank said on Wednesday.
About 78 percent of the assets, held by 36 local banks and 29 foreign banks, came from Asia and the rest from Europe and America, the bank said in a statement.
The bank said it had recently approved three more OBU applications for foreign banks and two more for local banks, seen as attractive because all OBU business is tax free.
In November, Taiwan's OBUs reported a monthly foreign exchange turnover of $4.053 billion, the statement said.

Of the derivatives operated by the OBUs, options trading accounted for $430 million, margin trading $403 million, interest rate swaps $299 million, financial futures $144 million and forward rate agreement $10 million, it said.
The government plans to expand OBU business as part of its scheme to become an Asia-Pacific financial operations centre.
